note: Written by Anne Bredon in the 1950s and known to Page from Joan Baez's 1962 recording. The first album credited it as traditional, arranged by Page. Later releases credit Anne Bredon with Page and Plant.

Jake Holmes recorded a song of the same name in 1967 and played it in New York on a bill with the Yardbirds, Page's band at the time. Holmes sued in 2010 and the case was settled. Celebration Day (2012) credits the song to Page, inspired by Jake Holmes.
Willie Dixon sued in 1985, saying the words drew on his song You Need Love, recorded by Muddy Waters in 1962. The case was settled and Dixon is now credited as a co-writer.
On stage in 1969 it was introduced as Killing Floor, a Howlin' Wolf song. After a settlement in the early 1970s, later releases credit Chester Burnett, Howlin' Wolf's real name.
The estate of Randy California of Spirit claimed the opening drew on the 1968 instrumental Taurus. A jury found no copyright infringement in 2016, and the verdict was upheld on appeal in 2020.
